clue.text: Devour a small boy — Mowgli, for instance

parts.note: to wolf food is to eat it greedily
a cub is a youngster, a young lad

explanation.surface: A grim tale of a beast eating a child, with Kipling's jungle boy cited as the example.
explanation.walkthrough: Mowgli, in Kipling's The Jungle Book, was raised by wolves; Wolf Cubs were also the junior branch of the Scouts.
explanation.definitionFit: Mowgli was brought up among wolves as one of their young, an example of a young wolf.

clue.text: What I left is off, anyway

indicators.note: something off has gone bad or awry, so these letters are thrown out of order

explanation.surface: Someone notes that whatever they left behind has gone off regardless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is off' rearranges WHAT and I into WITHA; L for 'left' then follows. 'off' looks like 'gone bad' but signals the shuffle.
explanation.definitionFit: Withal is an old adverb meaning nevertheless or in any case, the same as anyway.

clue.text: Lengthen Strand

explanation.surface: Two bare words that look like instructions about hair or rope.
explanation.definitionFit: A dressmaker lets down a hem to lengthen a garment; to leave someone stranded is to fail or abandon them.

clue.text: Plant a clue, and start to look puzzled

indicators.note: puzzled means confused, so the letters are jumbled
the start of a word is its opening letter

explanation.surface: A setter plants a clue and starts to look baffled by it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'start to' gives L from 'look'; 'puzzled' rearranges A, CLUE, AND and that L. 'Plant' looks like a verb but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Calendula is the pot marigold, a garden flower.

clue.text: A supposed benefit of taking early retirement?

definitions.text: A supposed benefit of taking early retirement?

parts.words: A supposed benefit of taking early retirement?
parts.note: retirement here is going to bed, not leaving work; an early night is said to improve your looks

explanation.surface: A remark on the perks of quitting work young.
explanation.definitionFit: Sleep before midnight is popularly held to keep one looking attractive and fresh.

clue.text: River in Rome where Caesar overcame Nervii initially

indicators.note: one piece is placed within the other
takes the opening letter of each of the four words

parts.note: ubi is the Latin word for where, as spoken in Rome

explanation.surface: A history lesson: the river near Rome where Caesar beat the Nervii tribe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' gives R, C, O, N from Rome, Caesar, overcame, Nervii; 'in' puts UBI (Latin for 'where') after the R. Caesar actually crossed this river into Italy, not fought the Nervii there.
explanation.definitionFit: The Rubicon is the stream in northern Italy that Julius Caesar crossed in 49 BC.

clue.text: May it give aroma to a Marseille street?

explanation.surface: A whimsical question whether some herb perfumes a street in Marseille.
explanation.definitionFit: Rue is a strongly scented herb; in French the word for a street is rue.

clue.text: Surface may be wet or dry at College

parts.note: at Eton a wet bob rows and a dry bob plays cricket, so a bob may be either
up means in residence at university, as in up at Oxford

explanation.surface: A remark that a surface might be damp or dry at some college.
explanation.walkthrough: Eton slang: pupils are wet bobs (rowers) or dry bobs (cricketers). 'Surface' is a verb here.
explanation.definitionFit: To surface is to rise back to the top of water, which is what a float does when it pops up.

clue.text: Peacock took apple and honey

parts.note: Cox's Orange Pippin, usually just Cox, is a popular English apple
honeycomb, shortened to comb, is the wax structure holding honey

explanation.surface: A peacock helps itself to apple and honey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Peacock' is a vain, showy man here, not the bird; 'took' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A coxcomb is a vain dandy, a strutting fop, just as a showy man is called a peacock.

clue.text: Scandinavians, and not people from Kent

parts.note: nor means and not
Kent is in south-east England, so its people are SE men

explanation.surface: Scandinavians are contrasted with the men of Kent.
explanation.walkthrough: Kent is a county in the South-East (SE) of England.
explanation.definitionFit: Norsemen were the medieval people of Scandinavia, the Vikings.

clue.text: Twist it a little to turn on

indicators.note: twisting distorts something, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Advice to twist a knob slightly to switch something on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Twist' rearranges IT A LITTLE; 'turn on' means arouse, not switch on.
explanation.definitionFit: To titillate is to excite or arouse, a slang sense of turn on.

clue.text: Pug, or another dog

explanation.surface: A pug, or failing that some other breed.
explanation.definitionFit: A pug is short for pugilist, a fighter in the ring; a boxer is also a breed of dog.

clue.text: Goodness found in a new fruit

indicators.note: one piece is discovered sitting inside another

parts.note: cor is a British exclamation of surprise, like goodness

explanation.surface: Something nutritious discovered in a novel fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'found in' puts COR inside A + N.
explanation.definitionFit: An acorn is the nut of the oak, botanically its fruit.

clue.text: Hope, in its destruction, becomes fury

indicators.note: the letters are broken up and rebuilt

explanation.surface: When hope is destroyed it turns into rage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'destruction' rearranges HOPE, IN, ITS; 'fury' is a proper noun in disguise.
explanation.definitionFit: Tisiphone was one of the three Furies, avenging goddesses of Greek myth.

clue.text: Vessel on the open wave a naval destroyer?

parts.note: a ship is a vessel
a breaker is a large wave crashing in open water

explanation.surface: A ship riding the waves is a warship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a naval destroyer' is not a warship but someone who breaks up old ships for scrap.
explanation.definitionFit: A shipbreaker demolishes old ships, literally a destroyer of naval craft.

clue.text: Incompetent to comprehend issue beyond doubt

indicators.note: comprehend in its sense of include or contain, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: unable means incompetent
a question is an issue under discussion

explanation.surface: Someone too incompetent to grasp an issue that is beyond doubt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to comprehend' uses comprehend's old sense of include or take in, not understand.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unquestionable is certain, admitting no dispute.

clue.text: Races, and their members

explanation.surface: Peoples, and those belonging to them.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition leans on the first: the members of races (nations) are their citizens.
explanation.definitionFit: The Grand National and similar events are horse races called nationals; citizens of a country are its nationals.

clue.text: Minister is outspoken after tea

parts.note: cha is slang for tea
plain-spoken, blunt

explanation.surface: A clergyman speaks his mind once tea is over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Minister' is a clergyman, not a politician; 'is' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A chaplain is a clergyman attached to an institution, a minister of religion.

clue.text: Find comfort in bed, having trouble with drink

parts.note: to be in hot water is to be in trouble
the bottle means alcoholic drink, as in hit the bottle

explanation.surface: Someone takes to drink in bed when in trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Find' and 'having' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: A rubber container of heated water warms the sheets, a source of cosiness at night.

clue.text: From which soldiers drank when intoxicated?

definitions.text: From which soldiers drank when intoxicated?

parts.words: From which soldiers drank when intoxicated?
parts.note: tank soldiers, or anyone tanked up, drink from a large beer mug

explanation.surface: A question about the vessel troops used when drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: Plays on 'tanked' meaning drunk and 'tank' crews as soldiers.
explanation.definitionFit: A tankard is a large drinking mug, usually for beer.

clue.text: Rather brave when head is chopped off — it's better off

indicators.note: the first letter of the word is removed

parts.note: pluckier means braver, more courageous

explanation.surface: Someone brave enough to be beheaded is supposedly better off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when head is chopped off' removes the P of PLUCKIER.
explanation.definitionFit: Luckier means more fortunate, in a better position.

clue.text: Not familiar with virgin

explanation.surface: Two definitions laid side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: Unused to something means unaccustomed to it; unused also means new, untouched, like virgin snow.

clue.text: Bananas, unopened, are still fruit

parts.note: remove the first letter of the word bananas and what is left is the French name for a tropical fruit

explanation.surface: Bananas still in their skins remain fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: Without its B, 'bananas' becomes ANANAS, the word for this fruit in French and many other languages.
explanation.definitionFit: The pineapple is the tropical fruit of the plant Ananas comosus.

clue.text: Gladstone's declaration in self-defence?

parts.note: Gladstone led the Liberals, so his self-description might be the article, the party's short name, then the first-person pronoun; that statement doubles as a plea of being elsewhere

explanation.surface: A Victorian Prime Minister's speech justifying himself.
explanation.walkthrough: W. E. Gladstone led Britain's Liberal Party, whose members are 'Libs'; split the answer after its first letter and again before its last.
explanation.definitionFit: An alibi is a claim of having been somewhere else, offered to defend oneself against a charge.

clue.text: Love a quick read of old Italian

parts.note: love is nil in tennis, the letter O
to scan is to read quickly

explanation.surface: A romantic skims a book about an ancient Italian.
explanation.definitionFit: Oscan was an ancient language of southern Italy, related to Latin.

clue.text: Old craftsman's dramatic discovery

indicators.note: the answer is found lying within the word that follows

explanation.surface: An antique maker makes a sensational find.
explanation.walkthrough: The run sits inside 'dramatic'; ''s' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The Amati family of Cremona were celebrated violin makers of the 16th and 17th centuries.

clue.text: Get married and be offended

explanation.surface: A wedding and a huff in one breath.
explanation.walkthrough: The first sense is a pun: to take a Miss as a wife.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking a young unmarried woman is marrying; to take something amiss is to resent it.

clue.text: Mount sheep?

parts.note: in a down entry the word read upward gives get up, which means mount

explanation.surface: A question about sheep from a hill, or climbing onto one.
explanation.walkthrough: A teg is a sheep in its second year; read from the bottom, the entry is GET, so it is 'get up'.
explanation.definitionFit: A teg is a two-year-old sheep, and climbing onto a horse is getting up.

clue.text: Giving a salute, without being at attention?

explanation.surface: Someone acknowledges others while dozing.
explanation.definitionFit: A bow of the head is a greeting; to nod off is to drift asleep, losing attention.

clue.text: Petra's colour will be dry — stick around

parts.note: a rod is a stick
sere means dried up, withered

explanation.surface: Someone will have a dry stick hanging around Petra.
explanation.walkthrough: Petra in Jordan is 'a rose-red city half as old as time' in J. W. Burgon's poem; 'will be' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The poem calls the ancient city's sandstone a pinkish-red hue.
